paper_title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Selecting intermediate features from a frozen diffusion model for discriminative tasks is non-trivial because the useful signal is distributed across the denoising trajectory, network depth, and channels. In practice, this requires choosing a timestep, a block, and a channel subset. Existing methods either fix these choices by hand or optimize only a few extraction hyperparameters, most often the timestep, then reuse the same rule across inputs and budgets. We introduce Policy-Mask, a budget-conditioned policy trained on the downstream objective that jointly selects all three under a prescribed channel budget. Without normalization, the channel-score contribution grows with the number of selected channels and dominates the timestep and block updates. We normalize it by subset cardinality, keeping the three policy heads on comparable scales and stabilizing joint training. At matched budgets, Policy-Mask improves over fixed extraction and feature-filter baselines across segmentation, classification, and semantic correspondence, reaching 38.9 mIoU on ADE20K, 75.4% top-1 on CIFAR-100 at 128 dimensions, and 76.3 PCK@0.1 on SPair-71k. Component-wise ablations show that block selection materially affects downstream accuracy, and the highest recorded channel-budget score occurs at 256 retained channels, identifying a practical operating point for compact diffusion representations. We further adapt Policy-Mask to diffusion transformers, including PixArt-$Σ$ and SD3.5 MMDiT, by replacing U-Net channels with image-token hidden dimensions.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Diffusion models learn intermediate representations that support semantic segmentation, image classification, and semantic correspondence (Baranchuk et al., 2022; Xiang et al., 2023; Tang et al., 2023). Using these representations for downstream task requires choosing which activations to extract. The available features depend on the denoising timestep and network layer, and each feature map contains set of channels from which the task representation is formed. Existing methods address this choice through fixed extraction rules, learned aggregation across timesteps and layers, or timestep selection during distillation (Luo et al., 2023; Yang & Wang, 2023). RepFusion transfers features from frozen diffusion teacher to student and learns which timestep to use. This leaves the choice of layer and retained feature dimensions as further parts of the extraction problem. These choices also determine which activations must be stored and used as distillation targets. POLICY-MASK selects timestep, layer, and channel subset under prescribed channel budget. The policy takes the input image and budget and selects an action = (t, l, K) with = b. task decoder provides the selection reward, and the selected features supervise the student during training. At inference, the student processes the image without evaluating the diffusion teacher. This extends RepFusions timestep selection to joint choice of extraction point and feature subset. Our contributions are: 1. budgeted (t, l, K) policy with exact-cardinality sampling. 2. channel-score normalization that controls the relative action-head contributions. 3. At 128 of 1280 aligned channels, gains of 1.21.6 mIoU over full-width fixed extraction on four segmentation benchmarks. 4. formal action mapping from U-Net features to DiT, MMDiT, and flow transformer feature lattices. Section 2 reviews related work, Section 3 defines the policy, Section 4 reports experiments, and Section 5 concludes. Appendices AC provide experimental details and additional results.

sections.title: 2 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Diffusion representations. Diffusion features support dense prediction, correspondence, segmentation, and depth estimation through task-specific extraction rules (Baranchuk et al., 2022; Xiang et al., 2023; Yang & Wang, 2023; Luo et al., 2023; Tang et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2023; Ji et al., 2023; Xu et al., 2023; Li et al., 2023; Ke et al., 2024). Recent work studies prompt selection, noisefree representations, and the transfer of stable diffusion to dense tasks (Li et al., 2024; Tian et al., 2024; Kondapaneni et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024; Stracke et al., 2025; Ravishankar et al., 2025). RepFusion is the closest predecessor: it distills recognizer from frozen diffusion teacher after selecting useful noise step (Yang & Wang, 2023). POLICY-MASK keeps the same teacherstudent division and expands the selected object to (t, l, K). Budgeted subset selection. Feature selection spans filters, wrappers, continuous relaxations, and greedy methods (Peng et al., 2005; Kohavi & John, 1997; Abid et al., 2019; Das & Kempe, 2011; Elenberg et al., 2018; Mirzasoleiman et al., 2015; Nemhauser et al., 1978). POLICY-MASK selects feature dimensions of one frozen model response. Budget-conditioned policies also appear in diffusion caching, where ReCache selects recomputation steps under an inference budget (Aliev et al., 2026). Here the budget constrains feature coordinates used for distillation. The policy uses PlackettLuce ordering and Gumbel top-b sampler (Plackett, 1975; Kool et al., 2019). Its gradient estimator follows the standard score-function construction with baseline (Greensmith et al., 2004; Kool et al., 2020).

sections.title: 4 EXPERIMENTS
sections.content: 4.1 EXPERIMENTAL SETUP Teacher and student. The main selector comparisons use frozen SD-1.5 U-Net and common width of 1280 aligned channels. Compact selectors retain 128 channels. The student loss and updates are given in Equation 2 and Algorithm 1. Datasets and metrics. Segmentation is evaluated on ADE20K (Zhou et al., 2017), Cityscapes (Cordts et al., 2016), CelebA-HQ (Karras et al., 2018), and Pascal VOC (Everingham et al., 2010) using mIoU. Classification uses CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (Krizhevsky, 2009) top-1 accuracy. Semantic correspondence uses SPair-71k (Min et al., 2019) PCK@0.1 with image and bounding-box normalization reported separately. Baselines. The baselines include fixed extraction, top-variance and Fisher channel selection, and full-width extraction. The DDAE (Xiang et al., 2023) and RepFusion (Yang & Wang, 2023) entries in Table 2 retain their corresponding source protocols. 4.2 MAIN RESULTS At 128 selected channels, POLICY-MASK exceeds full-width extraction at fixed (t, l) by 1.5, 1.6, 1.2, and 1.3 mIoU on ADE20K, Cityscapes, CelebA-HQ, and Pascal VOC, respectively  (Table 1)  . sections.title: 5 CONCLUSION
sections.content: We presented POLICY-MASK, which treats diffusion feature extraction as budgeted decision: policy jointly selects the timestep, the layer, and an exact-size channel subset of frozen teacher, and the selected features distill student that runs alone at inference. The experiments support three conclusions. First, joint selection pays off at fixed budget: with 128 of 1280 channels, POLICYMASK exceeds full-width extraction at fixed extraction point on all four segmentation benchmarks and exceeds RepFusion on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Second, channel-score normalization improves the tested joint policy. Without the 1/b factor, the joint policy falls below the timestep-only policy in the action-axis ablation. With fixed alignment, normalization raises ADE20K mIoU from 36.8 to 37.7 over three seeds. Third, the action transfers to DiT and MMDiT teachers by replacing U-Net channels with image-token hidden dimensions while retaining the student loss and exactcardinality constraint. Separating channel count from distillation strength remains the main open question for choosing the operating budget.

sections.title: A EXPERIMENTAL DETAILS
sections.content: A.1 CHANNEL-BUDGET SWEEP Figure 2 compares channel budgets on ADE20K using top-magnitude selection at fixed timestep and layer, with separate student trained for each budget. The highest validation mIoU is obtained at = 256. The masked distillation loss is averaged over all 1280 channels, so changing the budget also changes its scale. This experiment does not isolate the effect of channel count from the change in distillation strength. A.2 FIXED ALIGNMENT With trainable Al, the KD loss fell below 0.005 within two epochs in each diagnostic run. This behavior is consistent with projection shrinkage toward zero. We therefore fixed Al for the channelscore normalization ablation and the RepFusion comparison.

B.1 FIXED-SLOT REFERENCE RUNS Table 4 compares feature selection methods on ADE20K at fixed timestep and layer. The fullwidth baseline uses 1280 channels, while random and top-variance selection retain 128 channels. These 14-epoch reference runs follow separate protocol and are not compared numerically with Table 1. B.2 CHANNEL-SCORE NORMALIZATION AND REPFUSION COMPARISON The normalized and unnormalized policies use fixed Al, the same seeds, and the same training settings. They differ only in the 1/b channel-score factor. Our ADE20K implementation of RepFusion uses SD-1.5 and follows two stages: feature distillation followed by segmentation training. The teacher-side alignment remains fixed. RepFusion uses all 1280 dimensions, while POLICY-MASK retains 128. QUALITATIVE AND CLASS-WISE ANALYSIS The seed-0 comparison covers 2000 ADE20K validation images. POLICY-MASK has higher imagemIoU than RepFusion on 39.1% of images. This image-level comparison is separate from the dataset mIoU reported across three seeds. Class IoU improves for ball, flag, bridge, sand, monitor, and mountain, with losses for sconce, sink, animal, and desk (Figure 5).
